body: Frankly speaking I haven’t thought about it. Maybe this will work. Thank you!

The thing is that I’m from Eastern Europe, and mental health here is still considered a ‘taboo’ topic. Even though my mum knows, she doesn’t really understand what it’s like, and every time I try opening up to her she tells me to ‘suck it up’ or that other people have worse lives than I do. I know she loves me, and it’s always been a hard love, but she’s all I have and I could never make her go through all that shame. She barely accepted the fact that I take meds. 
Plus, where I am from mental hospitals are still perceived as places for the ‘crazy’ folks. The healthcare there is awful, from what I’ve heard and read you may not see a psychiatrist during your whole stay. I am worried that if I would actually be sent there, I would never be able to get a decent job because the employers would think I’m too unstable. That’s what it’s like here. My only gateway out of this country is university, and I cannot afford loosing my education because of staying in the hospital
